notes: Carvedilol Prospective Randomized Cumulative Survival. Severe HF (EF <25%). Carvedilol: Reduced mortality 35% (16.4% vs 22.1%, HR 0.65). STOPPED EARLY. Established beta-blockers even in severe HF. NEJM.
Carvedilol Or Metoprolol European Trial. Chronic HF. Carvedilol: Reduced mortality 17% vs metoprolol (34% vs 40%, HR 0.83, p=0.0017). Carvedilol superior to short-acting metoprolol. Lancet.

Systolic Heart failure treatment with the If inhibitor ivabradine Trial. HFrEF + HR ≥70 bpm on beta-blocker. Ivabradine: Reduced CV death/HF hosp 18% (24% vs 29%, HR 0.82). Heart rate reduction beneficial. Lancet.

Vericiguat Global Study in Subjects with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction. Recent HF worsening. Vericiguat: Reduced CV death/HF hosp 10% (35.5% vs 38.5%, HR 0.90, p=0.02). Modest benefit in worsening HF. NEJM.

Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure. HFrEF. Omecamtiv: Reduced CV death/HF events 8% (37.0% vs 39.1%, HR 0.92, p=0.03). First cardiac myosin activator. NEJM.

Digitalis Investigation Group. HF + normal sinus rhythm. Digoxin: NO mortality benefit (34.8% vs 35.1%, RR 0.99) BUT reduced HF hospitalization (26.8% vs 34.7%). Symptom control without mortality benefit. NEJM.

Randomized Aldactone Evaluation Study. Severe HF (NYHA III-IV). Spironolactone: Reduced mortality 30% (35% vs 46%, RR 0.70). STOPPED EARLY. Landmark MRA trial. Established aldosterone antagonism in HF. NEJM.

Treatment of Preserved Cardiac Function Heart Failure with an Aldosterone Antagonist. HFpEF. Spironolactone: NO mortality benefit (18.6% vs 20.4% death, p=0.14). Reduced HF hosp. Neutral trial for HFpEF. NEJM.

Eplerenone in Mild Patients Hospitalization And SurvIval Study in Heart Failure. Mild HFrEF (NYHA II). Eplerenone: Reduced CV death/HF hosp 37% (18.3% vs 25.9%, HR 0.63). STOPPED EARLY. Extended MRA benefit to mild HF. NEJM.
